chapter: Politics, bebop and the small-band years
title: Meeting Dizzy Gillespie in Philadelphia
summary: Crawford says he met Dizzy in Philadelphia, credits him with bringing in bebop, and calls him a great all-around trumpeter who could swing.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Yeah, he still sounds beautiful. So did you have occasion to play with any of the bebop musicians, like Dizzy Gillespie or Charlie Parker?
No. No, I think I played with Dizzy, but not the rest of them -- Charlie Parker and Bud Powell and all them, no.
You knew Dizzy Gillespie fairly well, didn't you?
Was he still in Cab Calloway's band when you met him?
No, he was just gigging by himself. He's responsible for bringing in bebop. He and Charlie Parker. But Dizzy was the man, he's a great trumpet player.
Did you think he swung in bebop style?
I didn't want to hear that. Again. What did you say?
Did you think that within the bebop style, that Dizzy was swinging?
Yeah, in his type of way, he could swing. He was an all-around trumpet player.
